Metadata.title: LivingBots | Indie game studio behind Arcanes
Metadata.description: LivingBots is an indie game studio from Natal, Brazil. Now developing Arcanes, a pixel-art metroidvania with a world open to exploration. Play the demo in your browser.
Metadata.aboutDescription: Igor Felipe is the developer behind LivingBots: games, websites and technical guidance for teams building with AI. Here is how to work with me.

Hero.tagline: A pixel-art metroidvania with a world open to curiosity, RPG classes and combat shaped by the weapon in your hand.

Arcanes.label: Current project
Arcanes.heading: Go anywhere. Survive what you can.
Arcanes.lead: Arcanes is a metroidvania with a heavy focus on exploration. The maps aren't stages unlocked in a set order: the world is open from the very first minute, and you can wander into places you don't yet have the skills to survive.
Arcanes.body: Monsters drop items you collect and sell, and that loot becomes the gold that upgrades your gear. On top of it sit an RPG class system, equipment refining and combat styles that change with the weapon you carry and how you use it.

explore.title: A world that doesn't wait for permission
explore.desc: Valleys with living water reflections, forests that swallow the light, caves under Eons. Every path is open. The only thing stopping you is whether you're strong enough yet.

fight.title: Your weapon is your playstyle
fight.desc: Swords, daggers and shields, each with its own rhythm. Block, parry, strike from behind. How you fight is a choice you keep making, not a menu you pick once.

gear.title: Loot becomes power
gear.desc: What monsters leave behind is your economy. Sell it, refine your swords, daggers, armor and shields, and walk back into the place that beat you.

World.label: The story
World.heading: Found in the heart of an oak
World.p1: Long before the Great Rupture, Luffendor was whole, and Lunethiel, the elven city among the ancient trees, stood at its height.
World.p2: Ages later, an elven king and his daughter find a human baby alone inside the trunk of a sacred oak. They name him Lyff and raise him as one of their own, in the wisdom, culture and customs of the Lunethi.
World.p3: Grown, Lyff begins his training as a Lunethi warrior. But the further he travels, the clearer it becomes: his origins, and his destiny, hide far more than he was ever told.

Studio.label: The studio
Studio.heading: LivingBots is one developer with a lot of stubbornness.
Studio.copy: I'm Igor Felipe, and I've been writing code for 16 years. From Natal, Brazil, I make games I'd want to get lost in, and I help other people build theirs.

About.label: About
About.heading: Hi, I'm Igor.
About.lead: I'm the developer behind LivingBots, a one-person game studio from Natal, Brazil. I've been writing software for 16 years, and these days most of my hours go into Arcanes.
About.p1: I like breaking ambitious ideas into milestones small enough to actually ship. That's how Arcanes went from a sketch to a playable demo in the browser, and it's how I work with anyone who hires me.
About.p2: Arcanes isn't a solo effort in everything: Heloiza runs our social media and Felipe takes care of the community. The code, the pipelines and most late nights are mine.

Work.label: Work with me
Work.heading: How we can work together
Work.intro: Whether it's a game, a website or a codebase that's started to fight back, I work in short, visible checkpoints, so you always know what's done and what comes next.

audit.title: One-time audit
audit.desc: I go through your project and hand you a clear report: what's broken, what's about to break, and the order to fix it in.

accompaniment.title: Ongoing accompaniment
accompaniment.desc: A recurring check-in on your codebase and decisions, so problems get caught while they're still small.

partnership.title: Build partnership
partnership.desc: I build with you, milestone by milestone, whether it's a game, a web product or a feature.

talk.title: Tell me what you're building
talk.desc: A short email is enough. I'll be honest about whether I'm the right person.

checkpoint.title: We agree on the first checkpoint
checkpoint.desc: Something small, concrete and useful. Not a six-month plan.

ship.title: I deliver, you review
ship.desc: Every checkpoint ends with something you can see, play or run.

Factory.label: Behind the scenes
Factory.heading: The Factory
Factory.intro: I'm building my own software factory: real GitHub issues go in one end, reviewed and tested code comes out the other. Inngest orchestrates the workflows, Claude Code implements them headless, and three deterministic gates (tsc, ESLint, Vitest) decide what reaches main. Failing work bounces back to the agent with feedback and gets carried through again. Untrusted branches run behind a trusted-ref adapter, so nothing escalates permissions.
